review_text: Delicate steamed dumplings filled with buttery leeks, topped with beef and split-pea tomato sauce, tangy lemon-garlic labneh, mint and cayenne. A vegetable sauce option is also available.
Flaky croissant filled with black sesame and almond frangipane, balancing sweetness with a subtle bitter edge. A striking black stripe is folded into the golden pastry.
Fluffy, slightly nutty buckwheat pancakes packed with juicy blueberries are a longtime Eastern Market favorite. Served with melting butter; the reviewer recommends the optional pure maple syrup.
A crisp-and-soft tortilla wrap filled with carne asada, queso, tortilla chips, chipotle aioli, vegetables and sour cream. The beef makes this fast-food homage feel like an upgrade.
A thick half-pound patty made from a custom dry-aged beef blend delivers buttery richness. Cracked pepper, cheddar, American cheese and onion complete the burger on a toasted housemade bun.
A thin, generously sized breaded chicken breast comes covered with mozzarella and basil. Request the rich, tangy vodka sauce, and save bread to soak up the extra.
Springy pork wontons scented with ginger shine in a complex chili-oil sauce with garlic and sweetened soy. The sauce balances sweetness, salt and lip-tingling heat without overwhelming spice.

A broiled, 10-ounce jumbo-lump crab cake uses mayonnaise as its binder without filler. Sweet crab, Old Bay and browned edges deliver simple richness; the article notes the crab is not Maryland-sourced.
Potato chips add crunch to this turkey-and-provolone sub. Shredded lettuce, pickles, onion, garlic mayo, oil and vinegar supply freshness and a sharp, savory punch.

Green curry sponge cake, avocado sorbet and soursop mousse meet fish sauce caramel, finger lime and dill. The unusual savory-sweet dessert is light and refreshing, with flavors that unfold gradually.
Sweet bulgogi beef, fluffy fontina scrambled eggs, chives and spicy gochujang aioli fill butter-toasted milk bread. The indulgent sandwich combines a crisp exterior with a soft center.
Two smashed patties use a seven-cut beef blend enriched with bone marrow. American cheese, steamed onions, dill pickles and house sauce make this sesame-bun burger especially rich and juicy.
Warmly spiced scrambled eggs with tomato, pepper and onion get a subtle drizzle of honey. Served with a lentil sambusa and injera for scooping; allow time for preparation.
Batter-fried cod shares a sturdy flour tortilla with cherry tomato, kale, jalapeño, avocado and cilantro. Jalapeño-cucumber dressing gives this carefully composed taco a fresh, colorful finish.

A longstanding Italian sub layers mortadella, pepperoni, salami, ham, provolone and fontina with oregano. The recommended hot-pepper and hard-roll combination adds spice and protects the hearty filling for takeout.
This playful pizza translates a Big Mac into a pie, piling burger components beneath shredded lettuce and special sauce. The reviewer finds the unlikely combination surprisingly successful.
Small batches and four daily flavors keep this ice cream cart inventive, with options such as olive oil, basil or labneh. Each flavor has its own base; fresh sourdough cones add caramelized crunch.
Kale leaves fried in chickpea batter become crisp pakoras dressed with sweet yogurt and chutneys. Melon seeds and grapes finish a lively street-food dish with contrasting textures.
Boat-shaped Georgian bread holds melted sulguni cheese, butter and an egg yolk mixed tableside. The ajaruli version remains a particularly comforting, stretchy-cheese favorite.

A two-tier seafood spread pairs a dozen oysters with six large shrimp and jumbo-lump crab dijonnaise served with saltines. The reviewer highlights its value, especially at the article's half-price happy hour.

Rigatoni coated in glossy red sauce and housemade sausage gets depth from fennel seeds and fennel pollen. This enduring restaurant signature remains a favorite more than a decade after its earlier essential-dishes listing.
Warm, airy focaccia sandwiches thinly sliced Italian mortadella, creamy stracciatella and pistachio crema. Careful sourcing and a final olive-oil drizzle make the simple combination stand out.

Crisp coconut rice combines with herbs, scallions and peanuts in a lightly sweet fish-sauce dressing, with lettuce for wrapping. The reviewer especially recommends adding the optional fermented pork sausage.

review_text: Ube jam flavors a warm, springy bread pudding made with brown sugar and orange juice. Salted caramel, crunchy granola and a scoop of ube ice cream add richness and contrasting textures.
Chewy udon is coated in a parmesan and kombu-tea sauce, then topped with crisp prosciutto and an orange egg yolk. Stir the yolk through before eating for a richer sauce.

review_text: A seven-item vegetarian platter includes spicy lentils and stewed chickpeas. The reviewer recommends pairing it with special beef kitfo, raw steak dressed in herbed clarified butter and fiery mitmita spice.

Meat from several parts of a smoked whole pig is mixed with seasoning and cider-vinegar sauce, then finished with crushed fried skin. The reviewer favors skipping coleslaw to appreciate the pork's varied flavors.
